note: Page-section archetypes, and per section what makes it real rather than a placeholder. Written to give the Deliverable Acceptance gate (src/lib/services/deliverables/acceptance-contracts.ts) something concrete to check: that gate fail-closes on placeholder output, but today it only detects lexical tells ('your headline here', {{mustache}}, [ALL CAPS SLOT]). The `requires` and `placeholderTells` fields below are the semantic layer it does not yet have. Nothing here is wired into that gate — this is data waiting for a consumer.

sections.name: Hero
sections.purpose: State what this is and who it is for, above the fold.
requires: A specific noun for the product or service, not a category word
placeholderTells: A generic tagline with no object (e.g. 'Innovate. Grow. Succeed.')

sections.name: Problem
sections.purpose: Name the reader's situation in their own words before offering anything.
requires: At least one symptom the reader would recognize without explanation
placeholderTells: The product named before the problem lands

sections.name: Mechanism
sections.purpose: Explain why this works, not merely that it works.
requires: At least one step or component
A stated limit or edge case
placeholderTells: A three-step diagram whose steps are 'Sign up / Use it / Succeed'
No failure mode acknowledged anywhere on the page

sections.name: Proof
sections.purpose: Give the reader a reason to believe the mechanism section.
requires: At least one named source — a person, company, dataset, or dated measurement
A number with its unit and its timeframe
placeholderTells: A quote with no attributed name

sections.name: Offer
sections.purpose: State precisely what the reader gets and what it costs.
requires: A price, a range, or an explicit 'contact for pricing'

sections.name: Objection
sections.purpose: Answer the reason the reader is about to leave.
requires: At least one objection stated in the reader's voice, not softened
A direct answer, including 'no' where the answer is no
placeholderTells: Only objections the product happens to win
No objection section at all on a considered purchase

sections.name: FAQ
sections.purpose: Handle the logistics that would otherwise become support tickets.
requires: Questions a real buyer asks (delivery, cancellation, compatibility, data)
Answers that commit to something checkable
placeholderTells: Answers that restate the marketing copy

sections.name: Final CTA
requires: The same action as the hero, worded differently
A restated outcome, not a restated feature
placeholderTells: A different primary action than the hero, which splits intent
A countdown timer with no stated reason
